newsitem.title: JAPAN: Early introduction of 5-year JGBs seen uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Early introduction of 5-year JGBs seen uncertain.

text.p: A six-month-old medium-term yen bond futures market has been eagerly awaiting introduction of underlying cash bonds, but prospects have dimmed as a revision of the current fiscal debt plan is uncertain, traders said.

The market had expected the Ministry of Finance to unveil its plan for five-year coupon government notes later this year while drafting a supplementary budget and revising its debt plan for the year to March 31, 1997, they said.
But some government officials and politicians recently appeared to have veered away from talk of an extra government spending because it may worsen Japan's massive budget deficit.

Although the Bank of Japan's quarterly "tankan" survey on Wednesday showed unexpectedly poor business sentiment, Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said this would not prompt an immediate decision on the need for an extra budget this fiscal year.
Kubo said he would make a decision on that after an announcement in mid-September of Japan's gross domestic product for the April-June quarter.
Low liquidity of cash Japanese government bonds (JGBs) for delivery when the five-year JGB futures contract expires has limited its use since it was added to 10- and 20-year JGB futures in February.

Qualifying cash issues for delivery are JGBs with three to five years left until maturity. But among the qualifying issues, five-year coupon notes have not been introduced yet to protect five-year bank debenture issuers.
An early introduction of five-year JGBs had been expected since the ministry said last year that it was considering issuing such securities, bond traders said.

"We hardly use five-year JGB futures due to a lack of turnover," said a senior trader at a major Japanese securities house. He said things may get better if the ministry issues five-year JGBs regularly in substantial amounts because that will increase hedge demand.
The highest daily turnover of five-year JGB futures at the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) was 18,458 contracts on the day the new futures contract was listed on February 16.
But since then, daily turnover has declined each month and only 874 contracts were traded daily in July on average, TSE data shows.
A TSE official said the exchange has no immediate plan to boost activity of the medium-term JGB futures because there has been no request from participants.
